quests.instruction: Which citrus fruit is often cut in half and eaten with a spoon, section by section?
quests.hint: Think of a big citrus fruit with a slightly bitter edge.
quests.explanation: Grapefruit halves are often spooned out section by section. Limes are too small for that, and kumquats are eaten whole.
quests.funFact: A grapefruit knife has a curved blade that loosens the segments.

quests.instruction: Which fruit is often cut into wedges to squeeze over food or into a drink?
quests.hint: People squeeze it instead of biting it.
quests.explanation: Lime wedges are squeezed so the sour juice flavors food and drinks. Plums and figs are eaten as they are.
quests.funFact: Lime juice is used to flavor food and drinks in many countries, from Mexico to Thailand.

quests.instruction: A peeled orange has soft white threads clinging to its segments. Is it okay to eat them?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, they are safe but can taste a bit bitter
options: No, they are harmful and must always be removed
Yes, but they must be cooked before eating
Yes, they are safe but can taste a bit bitter
quests.hint: Think about what that white layer is called in citrus fruits.
quests.explanation: The white threads are part of the pith. They are safe to eat, although they can taste a little bitter.
quests.funFact: The white threads carry water to the orange segments while the fruit grows.

quests.instruction: A grown-up slices two wide "cheeks" off the sides of this fruit, around its big flat stone. Which fruit is it?
quests.hint: The stone in the middle is long and flat, not round.
quests.explanation: A mango has a big flat stone in the middle, so the flesh is cut off in two wide pieces called cheeks.
quests.funFact: Scoring a mango cheek into squares and pushing it inside out makes it look like a hedgehog.

quests.instruction: A grown-up cuts this pink-skinned fruit in half so you can scoop out the flesh with a spoon. Which fruit?
quests.hint: Its skin is bright and scaly, and the spoon does the rest.
quests.explanation: Dragon fruit has a thick skin that is not eaten. The flesh and its tiny seeds are scooped out or sliced.
quests.funFact: The tiny black seeds of a dragon fruit are soft enough to eat.

quests.instruction: A lychee has a shiny brown seed inside. What should you do with it?
quests.correctAnswer: Spit it out or set it aside
options: Swallow it whole with the flesh
Chew it up with the flesh
Spit it out or set it aside
quests.hint: The seed is hard and not meant for eating.
quests.explanation: Lychee flesh is juicy and sweet, but the seed is hard and is not eaten.
quests.funFact: Longan and lychee are close relatives.

quests.instruction: Whole grapes can be hard for very young children to swallow safely. What can a grown-up do?
options: Freeze them until they are solid
Leave the stems on for a handle
quests.hint: Think about making each piece easier to chew.
quests.explanation: Grapes are the right size and shape to block a small child's throat, so a grown-up should cut them lengthways into smaller pieces.
quests.funFact: The same tip is used for cherry tomatoes and other small round foods.

quests.instruction: What should you do before touching fruit you are going to eat or share?
options: Wipe your hands on your shirt
quests.hint: Think about what is on your hands after playing.
quests.explanation: Washing your hands with soap helps keep germs off the fruit you are about to eat.
quests.funFact: Scrubbing for about twenty seconds is long enough to sing a short song twice.

quests.instruction: Many apples and pears have a tiny sticker on the skin. What should you do with it?
quests.correctAnswer: Peel it off and throw it away
options: Press it onto the next fruit
Peel it off and throw it away
quests.hint: Think about whether a sticker is food.
quests.explanation: Stickers help the shop identify the fruit, but they are not food, so remove them before eating.
quests.funFact: Those stickers often have a number that tells the cashier what kind of fruit it is.

quests.instruction: A big watermelon is cut into large triangle-shaped pieces for sharing. What are the pieces called?
quests.hint: Think of a slice of pizza.
quests.explanation: Wedges are triangle-shaped pieces cut from a round fruit.
quests.funFact: Wedges are easy for everyone to hold, which is why watermelon is often served that way.

quests.instruction: Mango is cut into small square pieces for a fruit salad. What are the pieces called?
quests.hint: Think of the shape of a dice.
quests.explanation: Cubes are small pieces with square sides, and mango cubes are easy to mix into a fruit salad.
quests.funFact: Cutting fruit into similar-sized pieces helps a fruit salad look neat and eat evenly.

quests.instruction: A grown-up cuts a pineapple into round slices with a hole in the middle. What are they called?
quests.hint: Think of something you wear on a finger.
quests.explanation: Pineapple rings are round slices with the tough core cut out of the middle.
quests.funFact: Apples can be sliced into rings too.

quests.instruction: A classmate says strawberries make them sick. What is a kind choice when you share fruit?
options: Ask them to try just one
quests.hint: Think about keeping your friend comfortable and safe.
quests.explanation: Some people have food allergies, so it is kind to listen and choose a different fruit for them.
quests.funFact: Many schools have snack rules so every child can enjoy food safely.

quests.instruction: Two friends want to share one apple fairly. What can they do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask a grown-up to cut it into two equal halves
options: Ask a grown-up to cut it into two equal halves
Take turns biting the same whole apple
One eats the whole apple while the other waits
quests.hint: Fair means both friends get the same amount.
quests.explanation: Cutting the apple into two equal halves gives each friend the same amount, and a grown-up keeps the knife safe.
quests.funFact: An apple can be cut into wedges so four or more friends can share.

quests.instruction: The thin skin around each pomelo segment is tough and bitter. What do many people do before eating?
options: Eat it as it is with the seeds
quests.hint: Think about getting to the juicy part inside.
quests.explanation: Pomelo segments are wrapped in a thin membrane that many people peel away to reach the juicy flesh.
quests.funFact: A pomelo can be as big as a small melon, so one fruit can feed many people.

quests.instruction: Which fruit is cooked like a vegetable when it is young and green, but eaten sweet when it is ripe?
quests.hint: Think of a huge spiky fruit that grows on a tree trunk.
quests.explanation: Young green jackfruit is cooked in savory dishes, while ripe jackfruit is sweet and eaten as a fruit.
quests.funFact: Unripe jackfruit is sometimes used as a meat substitute because of its stringy texture.

quests.instruction: Which fruit is often cooked into a sauce for pasta or curry?
quests.hint: It is red and grows from a flower, but people cook it with savory foods.
quests.explanation: Tomatoes are cooked into sauces for pasta, curries and many other dishes.
quests.funFact: Tomato sauces and curries are cooked in kitchens all over the world.

quests.instruction: Which fruit is too bitter to eat straight from the tree, so it is cured first?
quests.hint: Think of a small fruit with a pit that people soak or salt before eating.
quests.explanation: Fresh olives are very bitter, so they are soaked or cured before people eat them.
quests.funFact: Green and black olives can come from the same kind of tree and are picked at different times.

quests.instruction: Which fruit is often pressed through a sieve to make a smooth sauce without seeds?
quests.hint: Its many tiny seeds are hard to avoid.
quests.explanation: Raspberries have many tiny seeds, so cooks press them through a sieve for a smooth, seedless sauce.
quests.funFact: Raspberry sauce is a popular dessert topping in many countries.

quests.instruction: Which fruit is so delicate that it should be rinsed gently and handled with care?
quests.hint: Think of a fruit made of many soft, juicy bumps.
quests.explanation: Blackberries are made of many soft, juicy bumps that bruise easily, so they are rinsed gently.
quests.funFact: Blackberries are often picked by hand because they are so soft.

quests.instruction: Which fruit often makes a smoothie thick and creamy when it is blended?
quests.hint: Think of a soft fruit that mashes easily.
quests.explanation: Ripe banana is soft and blends into a thick, creamy texture. Grapefruit and cherries stay watery or chunky.
quests.funFact: Banana is a favorite smoothie fruit around the world.

quests.instruction: Taking the tough center out of an apple is called what?
quests.hint: Think about the word for the center of an apple.
quests.explanation: Coring means removing the tough center and the seeds from a fruit like an apple.
quests.funFact: A tool called a corer can remove an apple's core in one push.

quests.instruction: Taking the green leafy cap off a strawberry is called what?
quests.hint: Think about the name for the green cap.
quests.explanation: Hulling means removing the green cap, and the tough bit under it, from a strawberry.
quests.funFact: Some people use a small spoon or a straw to hull strawberries.

quests.instruction: Taking the hard stone out of a cherry or a plum is called what?
quests.hint: Think about the name for the hard center.
quests.explanation: Pitting means taking out the hard pit, or stone, from a fruit.
quests.funFact: A cherry pitter pushes the pit out through a small hole in one squeeze.

quests.instruction: What can you do with fruit peels and cores to help a garden?
quests.correctAnswer: Put them in a compost bin
options: Put them in a compost bin
quests.hint: Think about how food scraps can turn into soil food.
quests.explanation: Fruit peels and cores break down in a compost bin and become rich food for soil.
quests.funFact: Banana and orange peels break down in compost within a few weeks to months.

quests.instruction: You find black seeds in your watermelon slice. What can you do with them?
quests.correctAnswer: Put them aside on a napkin or plate
options: Flick them across the table to a friend
Put them aside on a napkin or plate
Swallow all of them in one gulp
quests.hint: Think about keeping the table tidy.
quests.explanation: Watermelon seeds can be set aside on a napkin or plate. Watermelon is still delicious without them.
quests.funFact: Roasted watermelon seeds are eaten as a snack in some countries.

quests.instruction: What is a safe way to eat fruit pieces?
quests.hint: Think about how to keep food from going down the wrong way.
quests.explanation: Sitting still and chewing slowly helps keep food from going down the wrong way.
quests.funFact: Taking small bites also helps you taste the fruit better.

quests.instruction: Custard apple flesh is soft and creamy, but its shiny black seeds are hard. What should you do with them?
quests.correctAnswer: Set them aside and do not eat them
options: Set them aside and do not eat them
Grind them into the fruit flesh
quests.hint: Think about the creamy part around the seeds.
quests.explanation: The seeds are hard and are not eaten. People scoop the creamy flesh around them.
quests.funFact: Custard apple is usually eaten with a spoon.

quests.instruction: When you eat tamarind, what is left behind?
quests.correctAnswer: The brittle pod and the hard seeds
options: The sticky pulp around the seeds
Nothing, all of it is eaten
The brittle pod and the hard seeds
quests.hint: Crack, scrape and nibble.
quests.explanation: People eat the sticky pulp and leave behind the brittle pod and hard seeds.
quests.funFact: Tamarind trees can live for a very long time.

quests.instruction: Which fruit has a leafy cap that is removed before you bite into it like an apple?
quests.hint: Think of a smooth orange fruit shaped a little like a flat tomato.
quests.explanation: Some persimmons, like the firm Fuyu type, can be eaten like apples once the leafy cap is removed.
quests.funFact: Persimmon trees keep their bright orange fruit even after their leaves fall in autumn.
